panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Ultrasound image of a human Pendred syndrome patient showing multiple hypoechoic thyroid nodules consistent with heterogeneous multinodular goiter, a classic clinical manifestation of the disease. B: MRI image of a human Pendred syndrome patient showing enlarged vestibular aqueduct, a characteristic inner ear malformation associated with the disease.

findings.evidence: Visible neck swelling consistent with multinodular goiter in the two older siblings, aligning with the in-text report of multinodular goiter on physical examination for all four patients

panels.rationale: Clinical photograph of four adolescent siblings with confirmed Pendred syndrome, demonstrating severe short stature and visible multinodular goiter, core clinical manifestations of the disease as described in the associated case report.
panels.attribution_text: Kara et al. Congenital goitrous hypothyroidism, deafness and iodide organification defect in four siblings: Pendred or pseudo-Pendred syndrome?. Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology 2010. doi:10.4274/jcrpe.v2i2.81. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Four siblings with severe short stature caused by congenital goitrous hypothyroidism
in_text_mentions: Four siblings presented with main complaints of short stature and deaf−mutism at ages ranging between 10.5 and 17.3 yrs (Figure 1). Their parents were cousins, and had no signs of hypothyroidism, goiter or hearing loss. Besides congenital deafness, the patients had mental and developmental delay. We could not measure their mental levels, because they could not speak. Their growth had also been retarded since birth. On physical examination, all four children had multinodular goiter and severe short stature. Their height SD scores were between −5.1 SD and −7.3 SD, and their bone ages were severe

plate_findings.evidence: caption: 'Ultrasound images of fetal goiter at 20.4 weeks gestation'; in-text: 'fetal goiter measuring 28 mm diameter'

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Real fetal 2D ultrasound panel from a case of fetal goiter with concomitant SLC26A4/thyroglobulin mutations (Pendred syndrome with congenital hypothyroidism); goiter is a direct captioned manifestation tied to the article's Pendred diagnosis. B: Second 2D ultrasound plane of the same fetal goiter case; human fetal patient image directly showing the captioned thyroid enlargement. C: 3D ultrasound rendering from the same fetal patient with goiter and confirmed SLC26A4/thyroglobulin mutations; qualifies as a human fetal imaging panel of the target disease manifestation.
panels.attribution_text: Calcaterra et al. Concomitant Mutations in the Thyroglobulin and SLC26A4 Genes Leading to Fetal Goiter and Congenital Hypothyroidism in a Patient With Pendred Syndrome.. Case reports in endocrinology 2025. doi:10.1155/crie/8797269. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Ultrasound images of fetal goiter at 20.4 weeks gestation. Panel A,B: ultrasound 2D sagittal (A) and longitudinal (B) planes; Panel (C) 3D ultrasound.
in_text_mentions: A 25-years-old quintigravida of Egyptian origin, affected by insulin-dependent diabetes and subclinical nonimmune hypothyroidism, and poor obstetrical history without children, due to cervical incontinence was referred to our Fetal Therapy Unit at 20.4 weeks gestation for a fetal goiter measuring 28 mm diameter (Figure 1).
